Source corpus for the exec-output taint engine (TestExecTaintSources). Every
kind of spawn-output source reaches errors.New once, on its WANT line; a value
that only resembles a source must not trip. Every exec.Cmd is a source — no
binary is classed safe — so the spawns name "git" and the engine must give the
same verdict when TestExecTaintVerdictIgnoresBinaryName swaps it for "cargo".

-- sources.go --
package sources

import (
	"bufio"
	"bytes"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os/exec"
)

// output: Output's first result is the stream.
func output() error {
	out, err := exec.Command("git", "log", "-1").Output()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return errors.New(string(out)) // WANT taint
}

// combined: CombinedOutput interleaves both streams; same verdict.
func combined(c *exec.Cmd) error {
	out, _ := c.CombinedOutput()
	return errors.New(string(out)) // WANT taint
}

// stdoutPipe: a line read off StdoutPipe is the stream.
func stdoutPipe(c *exec.Cmd) error {
	r, _ := c.StdoutPipe()
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(r)
	for sc.Scan() {
		return errors.New(sc.Text()) // WANT taint
	}
	return nil
}

// stderrPipe: reading StderrPipe to the end is the stream.
func stderrPipe(c *exec.Cmd) error {
	r, _ := c.StderrPipe()
	b, _ := io.ReadAll(r)
	return errors.New(string(b)) // WANT taint
}

// exitStderr: with Stderr unset, Output keeps the child's stderr on the
// *exec.ExitError. Reading it is a source; the error itself renders only
// "exit status N", so wrapping it with %w is clean.
func exitStderr() error {
	_, err := exec.Command("git", "status").Output()
	var ee *exec.ExitError
	if errors.As(err, &ee) {
		return errors.New(string(ee.Stderr)) // WANT taint
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("git: %w", err)
}

// stdoutBuffer: whatever object is plugged into Cmd.Stdout receives the stream.
func stdoutBuffer(c *exec.Cmd) error {
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	c.Stdout = &buf
	if err := c.Run(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return errors.New(buf.String()) // WANT taint
}

// wrapped embeds *exec.Cmd; its promoted Output is exec's own method.
type wrapped struct{ *exec.Cmd }

func promoted(c *exec.Cmd) error {
	w := wrapped{c}
	out, _ := w.Output()
	return errors.New(string(out)) // WANT taint
}

// fake has its own Output. Sources are matched by identity, not by name, so
// this is not one.
type fake struct{}

func (fake) Output() ([]byte, error) { return []byte("literal"), nil }

func lookalike() error {
	out, _ := fake{}.Output()
	return errors.New(string(out))
}

-- alias.go --
package sources

import (
	"errors"

	x "os/exec"
)

// aliased: os/exec under another import name trips identically.
func aliased() error {
	out, _ := x.Command("git", "show", "HEAD").Output()
	return errors.New(string(out)) // WANT taint
}
